newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B shares down on late institutional trade.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares down on late institutional trade.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index closed slightly lower on Monday on institutional selling of a handful of counters late in the afternoon session, brokers said.
The B share index edged down 0.10 points, or 0.11 percent, to close at 89.79 as turnover expanded to HK$79.00 million from last Friday's HK$17.99 million.
Some institutions entered the market late in the afternoon and cut their positions in several counters, which pulled the index down, brokers said.
But some issues were also seen being supported by institutions, limiting the index's loss, they added.
One broker said there were some Chinese investors diverting their funds out of B share counters into the bullish A share market.
Chiwan Petroleum was the worst performer on selling by institutions, brokers said. The counter tumbled HK$0.18 or 5.14 percent to 3.32 on volume of 2.02 million shares.
Lizhu Pharmaceuticals followed with a decline of HK$0.09 or 3.01 percent to 2.90 after 18,000 shares were traded.
Dadonghai advanced HK$0.03 to HK$1.37 on trade of 2.16 million shares.
Television tube maker SEG traded the most on volume of 7.47 million shares and ended unchanged at HK$2.67. The heavy volume was probably created by institutional cross trading, brokers said.
The A share market saw bullish trade on Monday on speculative buying triggered in part by institutional demand for large-cap conglomerate China Baoan, brokers said.
The A share index climbed 13.10 points, or 4.16 percent, to close at 327.99, with turnover swelling to 13.22 billion yuan from 10.39 billion yuan on Friday.
The composite index rose 11.59 points, or 3.93 percent, to end at 306.81.
Baoan, which is mainly involved in real estate development, surged 1.38 yuan, or 23.79 percent, to 7.18 yuan, with trade volume hitting 162.49 million shares.
Building materials producer Shenzhen Universe soared on speculative demand, brokers said. The issue shot up 2.11 yuan, or 32.61 percent, to 8.58 yuan, making it the session's strongest performer.
Retailer Shaanxi Minsheng plunged 1.10 points, or 10.81 percent, to 9.08 yuan on profit-taking, brokers said.
